info.title: bowire
info.description: Bowire — standalone CLI + browser UI for the multi-protocol API workbench. Discover, invoke, record, mock, and replay across gRPC, REST, GraphQL, MQTT, SignalR, WebSocket, SSE, MCP, OData, and Socket.IO — every first-party plugin pre-bundled. Run `bowire --url …` for the browser UI or `bowire list/describe/call` / `bowire mock` for grpcurl-style scripting and recording replay.

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription: Bowire — multi-protocol API workbench. Run without a subcommand to launch the browser UI; run a subcommand (list / describe / call / mock / mcp / plugin / test) for scripting.

options.name: --enable-mcp-adapter
options.description: Expose discovered services as MCP tools. [default: False]

options.name: --update-check
options.description: Opt in to the daily plugin-update check (off by default). Bowire queries nuget.org once per day for newer versions of every installed sibling plugin and surfaces a count badge in the sidebar. Equivalent to Bowire:PluginUpdateCheck:Enabled=true. [default: False]

options.name: --auth-provider
options.description: Id of the IBowireAuthProvider plugin that should gate workbench access (e.g. 'oidc'). When unset, the workbench stays open — same as today's laptop default. When set, the named plugin must be installed (e.g. `bowire plugin install Kuestenlogik.Bowire.Auth.Oidc`) or Bowire fails fast. Provider-namespaced flags are read from Bowire:Auth:<id>:* — for OIDC: --auth-oidc-authority, --auth-oidc-client-id, etc. (forwarded as Bowire:Auth:Oidc:Authority / ClientId).

options.name: --lock-server-url
options.description: Disable URL editing in the UI. [default: False]

options.name: --telemetry
options.description: Enable OpenTelemetry self-observability (#29). Bowire emits traces + Bowire-domain metrics (bowire.invoke.count / duration / bowire.discover.count / bowire.plugin.load / bowire.mock.requests) through the canonical 'Kuestenlogik.Bowire' Meter and ActivitySource. Wire endpoint, headers, and protocol come from the standard OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_* env vars. Off by default — laptop installs stay quiet. [default: False]

options.name: --telemetry-strip-method-labels
options.description: When --telemetry is on, drop the high-cardinality service + method dimensions from emitted metrics. Shared multi-tenant installs (GDPR / HIPAA / SOX) almost always want this; private-network deploys usually leave it off so per-method breakdowns survive. [default: False]

options.name: --ai-provider
options.description: AI provider id for the workbench's chat / hint surface (#25 Phase 2). Default 'ollama' speaks the local Ollama HTTP API on 127.0.0.1:11434; LM Studio on :1234 works through the same client because the wire shape matches. Cloud connectors slot in via the same Microsoft.Extensions.AI IChatClient seam in Phase 3. Maps to Bowire:Ai:ProviderId.

options.name: --ai-endpoint
options.description: Override the AI provider's HTTP endpoint. Default 'http://localhost:11434' (Ollama). Set to 'http://localhost:1234' for LM Studio, or to a remote Ollama gateway when the model server runs on another host. Maps to Bowire:Ai:Endpoint.

options.name: --ai-model
options.description: Model name passed to the AI provider. Default 'llama3.2:3b' (Ollama's small + free model that runs on a laptop). Use `ollama pull <name>` first; LM Studio uses whatever model is currently loaded. Maps to Bowire:Ai:Model.

options.name: --plugin-dir
options.description: Override the plugin directory.

options.name: --map-basemap
options.description: Map widget basemap: 'osm' / 'satellite' / 'demotiles' / 'none', a tile URL with {z}/{x}/{y}, or a style.json URL. Default: 'demotiles'.

options.name: --disable-plugin
options.description: Skip a protocol plugin at startup. Repeat or comma-separate ('--disable-plugin grpc --disable-plugin signalr' or '--disable-plugin grpc,signalr'). Useful when a plugin DLL won't load or its discovery probe is too slow for the current host.

options.name: --disable-cli-command
options.description: Skip an auto-discovered CLI subcommand at startup. Mirrors --disable-plugin but for IBowireCliCommand contributions (scan / future plugin commands). Repeat or comma-separate.

commands.name: jwt
commands.description: JWT decode / tamper toolkit. Tier-2 anchor of the security-testing lane (see docs/architecture/security-testing.md).

commands.name: decode
commands.description: Decode a JWT and pretty-print the header + payload.

commands.name: tamper
commands.description: Produce a tampered JWT (alg:none downgrade, claim mutation, optional HS256 re-signing).

options.name: --alg-none
options.description: Downgrade the token to alg:none (drops the signature; the classic JWT bypass). [default: False]

options.name: --set
options.description: Mutate a payload claim: --set claim=value. Repeatable. Values parsed as JSON literals first (so --set exp=9999999999 lands as number) and fall back to string.

options.name: --secret
options.description: Re-sign with HMAC-SHA256 using this secret (overrides --alg-none). Useful when probing weak-secret-based JWT validation.

commands.name: fuzz
commands.description: Schema-aware fuzzing of a single field. Tier-2 anchor of the security-testing lane.

options.name: --target
options.description: Target base URL.

options.name: --template
options.description: Recording-style JSON file describing the request shape (httpVerb / httpPath / body).

options.name: --field
options.description: JSONPath into the request body identifying the field to fuzz (e.g. $.username or $.filter.id).

options.name: --payloads
options.description: Payload category: sqli / xss / pathtrav / cmdinj.

options.name: --force
options.description: Run even when the field's value-shape doesn't match the payload class (e.g. fuzz a numeric field with string payloads anyway). [default: False]

options.name: --timeout
options.description: Per-payload HTTP timeout in seconds. Default 30.

options.name: --allow-self-signed-certs
options.description: Accept self-signed certs on the target. [default: False]

options.name: --auth-header
options.description: Add an HTTP header to every fuzz request (typically Authorization: Bearer …). Repeatable.

commands.name: proxy
commands.description: Intercepting HTTP/HTTPS proxy. Tier-3 anchor of the security-testing lane (see docs/architecture/security-testing.md).

options.name: --port
options.description: Port the proxy listens on (point browser / client at it). Default 8888.

options.name: --api-port
options.description: Sidecar API port the workbench's Proxy tab reads captured flows from. Default 8889.

options.name: --capacity
options.description: Maximum number of flows retained in memory (FIFO eviction). Default 1000.

options.name: --no-mitm
options.description: Disable HTTPS interception — CONNECT requests are tunneled-and-rejected with 501. Default: MITM enabled. [default: False]

options.name: --ca-dir
options.description: Override the CA storage directory. Default: ~/.bowire (PFX + DER cert persisted there).

options.name: --export-ca
options.description: Copy the public CA certificate to this path (.crt) and exit. Install the file into your trust store to suppress client-side warnings during HTTPS interception.

commands.name: scan
commands.description: Run vulnerability templates against a target URL. The Tier-1 anchor of the security-testing lane (see docs/architecture/security-testing.md).

options.name: --target
options.description: Target base URL (e.g. https://api.example.com).

options.name: --templates
options.description: Directory of *.json vulnerability templates to run (Bowire format).

options.name: --template
options.description: Single template *.json file to run (combinable with --templates).

options.name: --nuclei
options.description: Directory of *.yaml Nuclei templates (projectdiscovery/nuclei-templates). Read alongside --templates; resolved against --target so {{BaseURL}}/{{Hostname}} etc. land on real probes.

options.name: --out
options.description: Write findings as SARIF 2.1.0 JSON to this path (for CI dashboards: GitHub Code Scanning, GitLab, Azure DevOps).

options.name: --severity
options.description: Minimum severity to report: low / medium / high / critical. Lower-severity templates still load but are reported as skipped.

options.name: --timeout
options.description: Per-probe HTTP timeout in seconds. Default 30.

options.name: --allow-self-signed-certs
options.description: Accept self-signed / untrusted TLS certs on the target. Off by default — use only when probing a known dev/staging cert. [default: False]

options.name: --no-builtins
options.description: Skip the built-in passive checks (TLS-version enumeration, version-disclosing headers, verbose-error detection). Built-ins run by default. [default: False]

options.name: --scope
options.description: In-scope hostname or glob (e.g. `api.example.com` or `*.example.com` — the leading `*.` matches sub-domains but NOT the apex). Repeat or comma-separate. Defaults to the target's own host, so accidental cross-host probes are blocked unless explicitly widened.

options.name: --auth-header
options.description: Add an HTTP header to every probe — typically `Authorization: Bearer <token>` or `X-Api-Key: <key>`. Repeatable for multiple headers (cookies, multi-header auth schemes). Without this flag, scans of authenticated APIs land on the login wall and the scanner reports misleading 'endpoint missing' findings.
